taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Solidago nemoralis and lists Texas in its native range. Keep currently accepted western segregates such as Solidago decemflora distinct rather than inheriting old broad concepts automatically.
look_here_first: Start low on the plant. Gray goldenrod is comparatively short and gray-hairy, with a densely pubescent stem and narrow spatulate-to-oblanceolate lower leaves that become smaller and narrower upward. Then check the usually one-sided, wandlike/recurving flowering branches.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Natural Purola Plants list. Travis — UT PRC herbarium specimen index. Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County field treatment. These three exact counties meet the project threshold.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not transfer records assigned to currently accepted Solidago decemflora or Solidago mollis into S. nemoralis without checking the taxon concept.

best_field_traits: usually shorter and less colony-forming than tall goldenrods
lower leaves oblanceolate to spatulate and narrowed into a winged petiole
upper leaves progressively smaller and narrower
flowering array often one-sided and wandlike or recurving
common in dry open prairie, caliche, glade, old-field, and roadside settings
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Solidago radula, S. nemoralis is more gray/strigose overall and usually has a more wandlike one-sided inflorescence; S. radula is conspicuously scabrous with broader lower leaves and a more compact terminal panicle.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Gray goldenrod combines persistent gray pubescence, narrower lower foliage, and a one-sided wandlike flowering array. Rough goldenrod is more stiffly scabrous and has a more compact terminal panicle.
